units.title: Un pedido sencillo
units.objective: Reconocer un pedido, una bebida y una petición cortés.

vocabulary.example: Would you prefer hot tea or a cold drink?
There is a sandwich in my lunch box.
The dog needs fresh water.
The children are drawing at the table.

units.strategy: Escucha primero qué quiere la persona; después identifica bebida y comida.
units.passage: Hello. I would like a small tea and a cheese sandwich, please. The sandwich is for my sister. I do not want coffee today. Can I have some water too? We can sit at this table near the window.

questions.prompt: What is the person doing?
options: Paying for a hotel
Ordering food and drinks
Buying a window
Inviting a teacher
questions.explanation: La persona pide comida y bebida; no está pagando alojamiento.
questions.evidence: I would like a small tea and a cheese sandwich, please.

questions.prompt: Who is the sandwich for?
options: The teacher
The speaker
The sister
The waiter
questions.explanation: La frase identifica directamente a la hermana.
questions.evidence: The sandwich is for my sister.

questions.prompt: What extra drink does the person ask for?
options: Coffee
Milk
Juice
Water
questions.explanation: La pregunta cortés solicita agua adicional; el café se rechaza.
questions.evidence: Can I have some water too?

units.title: La primera clase
units.objective: Identificar lugar, objeto y una instrucción sencilla.

vocabulary.example: Our teacher tells interesting stories.
I borrowed a book about birds.
May I borrow a pen to write my name?
Her sports bag is blue.

units.strategy: Busca la instrucción con please y distingue lo que debes abrir de lo que debes guardar.
units.passage: Good morning. My name is Helen, and I am your teacher. This is our English class. Please open your book. You need a pen, but you do not need your phone. Put your phone in your bag. We can start now.

questions.prompt: Where is Helen speaking?
options: In a clothes shop
In an English class
At a train station
In a restaurant
questions.explanation: Helen presenta la clase de inglés.
questions.evidence: This is our English class.

questions.prompt: What should students open?
options: Their bag
Their phone
Their book
The window
questions.explanation: La instrucción es abrir el libro, no el bolso.
questions.evidence: Please open your book.

questions.prompt: What does Helen want students to put away?
options: Their pen
Their book
Their chair
Their phone
questions.explanation: Guardar el teléfono permite empezar la actividad.
questions.evidence: Put your phone in your bag.

units.title: Cambiar de parada
units.objective: Entender un aviso breve con un cambio y su causa.

vocabulary.example: We caught a bus after the concert.
I study at the library on quiet afternoons.
Keep your ticket until the end of the journey.
The road goes through the forest.

units.strategy: La información después de today puede cambiar tu plan habitual.
units.passage: The number twelve bus usually stops outside the bank. Today, please wait outside the library instead. Workers are fixing the road near the bank. Your ticket is still valid. The bus leaves at ten thirty, so please be at the library five minutes before that.

questions.prompt: What is the announcement mainly about?
options: A new bus ticket price
A library closing permanently
A different bus stop today
A bank changing its name
questions.explanation: El aviso cambia la parada de hoy.
questions.evidence: Today, please wait outside the library instead.

questions.prompt: Where should passengers wait?
options: Inside the bank
Near the workers
At the ticket office
Outside the library
questions.explanation: La biblioteca sustituye a la parada del banco.
questions.evidence: please wait outside the library instead

questions.prompt: Why is the normal stop unavailable?
options: The road is being repaired
The bank has no tickets
The driver is late
The library is full
questions.explanation: La reparación de la calle explica el cambio.
questions.evidence: Workers are fixing the road near the bank.

units.title: Un mensaje para el picnic
units.objective: Comprender preparativos y una petición cotidiana.

vocabulary.example: They enjoyed a picnic by the lake.
This bread smells wonderful.
There are clean cups in the kitchen.
The garden looks greener when it rains.

units.strategy: Distingue lo que ya lleva quien habla de lo que pide a la otra persona.
units.passage: Hi, Sam. Our picnic is on Saturday at the park. I have bread and apples, and Rosa is bringing juice. Could you bring some cups? We are meeting at eleven, not twelve. Call me if it rains before you leave home.

questions.prompt: What is the message about?
options: A shopping trip on Sunday
A cooking lesson
Plans for a picnic
Plans to visit Rosa at home
questions.explanation: El contexto es organizar el picnic.
questions.evidence: Our picnic is on Saturday at the park.

questions.prompt: When are they meeting?
options: At twelve
At ten
At one
At eleven
questions.explanation: Se corrige explícitamente la hora de doce a once.
questions.evidence: We are meeting at eleven, not twelve.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker ask Sam to bring?
options: Cups
Apples
Bread
Juice
questions.explanation: La petición es traer vasos; otras personas ya aportan la comida y el zumo.
questions.evidence: Could you bring some cups?

units.title: La habitación preparada
units.objective: Seguir instrucciones de llegada y una excepción temporal.

vocabulary.example: The room has a comfortable sofa.
The travellers carried their bags downstairs.
I often eat fruit for breakfast.
He could not find the key to his car.

units.strategy: Escucha but y las alternativas: algo puede estar disponible aunque tu primera opción no lo esté.
units.passage: Welcome to the hotel. Your room will be ready at two this afternoon. You can leave your bags here while you explore the town. Breakfast is included, but it finishes at nine thirty. The restaurant is closed tonight, so we can show you a cafe nearby. Please come back to reception to collect your key.

questions.prompt: What is the speaker mainly doing?
options: Taking a dinner order
Advertising a town tour
Cancelling a reservation
Giving a guest arrival information
questions.explanation: Se explica qué puede hacer un huésped al llegar.
questions.evidence: Your room will be ready at two this afternoon.

questions.prompt: What is included?
options: Breakfast
Dinner tonight
A town tour
A cafe meal
questions.explanation: Solo se confirma que el desayuno está incluido.
questions.evidence: Breakfast is included

questions.prompt: Why does the speaker mention a cafe?
options: To explain where breakfast is served
To offer an alternative for dinner
To arrange collection of bags
To say where the key is kept
questions.explanation: El restaurante cierra esta noche; el café es una alternativa.
questions.evidence: The restaurant is closed tonight, so we can show you a cafe nearby.

units.title: Ayuda con el turno
units.objective: Reconocer el problema, la disponibilidad y una solicitud.

vocabulary.example: She made an appointment to see the optician.
His night shift ends before sunrise.
The manager welcomed the new colleague.
Please confirm that you received the parcel.

units.strategy: No confundas la hora de la cita con las horas en que alguien puede trabajar.
units.passage: Hi, Alex. I have a dentist appointment on Tuesday morning, so I cannot open the shop. Could you work my morning shift? I can take your Friday afternoon shift in return. The manager has said this is fine if you agree. Please send me a message this evening so I can confirm the change.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker want to arrange?
options: A new dentist appointment
A meeting with a customer
A permanent new job
A swap of work shifts
questions.explanation: Propone intercambiar turnos, no abandonar el trabajo.
questions.evidence: I can take your Friday afternoon shift in return.

questions.prompt: When can the speaker work for Alex?
options: Friday afternoon
Tuesday morning
Friday morning
This evening
questions.explanation: La disponibilidad ofrecida es el viernes por la tarde.
questions.evidence: I can take your Friday afternoon shift

questions.prompt: Why should Alex reply this evening?
options: So the shop can close forever
So the change can be confirmed
So the dentist can change the appointment
So the manager can find a new shop
questions.explanation: La respuesta permite confirmar el intercambio con tiempo.
questions.evidence: Please send me a message this evening so I can confirm the change.

units.title: La bicicleta reparada
units.objective: Identificar una recomendación y distinguir acciones necesarias de opcionales.

vocabulary.example: The driver checked the brakes before the trip.
A sharp stone damaged a tyre on the car.
Is this seat next to you free?
He is collecting his daughter from school.

units.strategy: Atiende a contrastes entre lo que funciona y lo que necesita atención.
units.passage: I have checked your bicycle. The brakes are working well, but the back tyre needs replacing. We can do that this afternoon. You asked about a new seat, too. The old one is safe, so there is no need to change it unless you find it uncomfortable. I suggest collecting the bicycle tomorrow morning, because the shop gets very busy just before we close.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the message?
options: To explain repair needs and collection
To sell a completely new bicycle
To cancel all repairs
To announce a shop closure
questions.explanation: Se informa sobre la reparación necesaria y cuándo recoger la bicicleta.
questions.evidence: The brakes are working well, but the back tyre needs replacing.

questions.prompt: Which part needs replacing?
options: The brakes
The back tyre
The seat
The front wheel
questions.explanation: El neumático trasero sí requiere cambio; el asiento no necesariamente.
questions.evidence: the back tyre needs replacing

questions.prompt: Why is tomorrow morning recommended?
options: The seat is unsafe until tomorrow
The brakes cannot be checked today
The shop is busy near closing time
The shop is closed this afternoon
questions.explanation: La recomendación evita la hora de mayor actividad, no una reparación adicional.
questions.evidence: because the shop gets very busy just before we close

units.title: Elegir un curso
units.objective: Entender condiciones de un curso y una recomendación adaptada.

vocabulary.example: The label lists all the ingredients.
Keep the rice in a dry container.
My grandmother keeps her recipes in a notebook.
My name is on the waiting list for a music lesson.

units.strategy: Anota la condición para participar, no solo los horarios.
units.passage: Our evening cooking course starts next month. You do not need experience, and we provide all the ingredients. Bring a container to take your food home. The Saturday course covers the same recipes, but places are already full. If you work late during the week, put your name on the Saturday waiting list rather than booking an evening class you cannot attend.

questions.prompt: What is the announcement mainly about?
options: Choosing a suitable cooking class
Buying cooking equipment
Opening a restaurant
Hiring an experienced chef
questions.explanation: El anuncio presenta el curso y orienta sobre la opción adecuada.
questions.evidence: Our evening cooking course starts next month.

questions.prompt: What must learners bring?
options: All the ingredients
A container
Their own recipes
Proof of cooking experience
questions.explanation: El centro proporciona ingredientes; el alumno lleva un recipiente.
questions.evidence: Bring a container to take your food home.

questions.prompt: What is advised for someone who works late?
options: Book the evening class anyway
Choose different recipes
Join the Saturday waiting list
Arrive after the evening class ends
questions.explanation: La recomendación evita reservar un horario al que no se puede asistir.
questions.evidence: put your name on the Saturday waiting list rather than booking an evening class you cannot attend

units.title: Un retraso explicado
units.objective: Seguir una explicación con causa, acción y consecuencia.

vocabulary.example: The bakery found a local supplier of flour.
The broken lamp arrived with a free replacement bulb.
The family is staying in temporary accommodation.
I learned to paint at a weekend workshop.

units.strategy: Separa el problema inicial de la solución temporal.
units.passage: I am calling about the desks your team ordered. The supplier has sent the wrong size, so we are arranging a replacement rather than delivering something you cannot use. The correct desks should arrive on Thursday morning. In the meantime, we can lend you folding tables at no extra charge. These are only a temporary solution, but they would let your workshop go ahead on Wednesday. Please tell us by lunchtime whether you would like us to bring them over.

questions.prompt: Why is the speaker calling?
options: To charge for damaged desks
To explain a delay and offer temporary furniture
To cancel the workshop
To ask the team to change offices
questions.explanation: La llamada presenta una solución temporal al retraso de los escritorios.
questions.evidence: In the meantime, we can lend you folding tables at no extra charge.

questions.prompt: When are the correct desks expected?
options: Wednesday
At lunchtime today
Thursday
Next Monday
questions.explanation: Thursday es la previsión de llegada; Wednesday corresponde al taller.
questions.evidence: The correct desks should arrive on Thursday morning.

questions.prompt: Why might the team accept the tables?
options: They would replace the desks permanently
They would reduce the original order size
They would make the supplier deliver earlier
They would allow Wednesday’s workshop to take place
questions.explanation: La ventaja es poder realizar el taller pese al retraso.
questions.evidence: they would let your workshop go ahead on Wednesday

units.title: El club de lectura cambia
units.objective: Distinguir una mejora organizativa de una obligación.

vocabulary.example: The interview has a new question-and-answer format.
The final chapter explains how the mystery ends.
All members receive a monthly email.
The bedrooms are upstairs.

units.strategy: Observa expresiones como you do not have to: descartan una obligación aparente.
units.passage: At our next book club meeting, we will try a different format. Instead of discussing every chapter together, we will start in small groups and then share our main ideas. Several members said they wanted more time to speak, and this should help. You do not have to finish the whole book to join us; reading the first three chapters is enough. We will keep the usual meeting time, but use the larger room upstairs so the groups have more space.

questions.prompt: What change is being introduced?
options: A meeting only for new members
Small-group discussion before sharing ideas
A different meeting day every week
Silent reading for the entire meeting
questions.explanation: La novedad es la organización de la conversación.
questions.evidence: we will start in small groups and then share our main ideas

questions.prompt: How much reading is required to join?
options: The entire book
Only the final chapter
The first three chapters
Two different books
questions.explanation: No es necesario terminar el libro completo.
questions.evidence: reading the first three chapters is enough

questions.prompt: What problem is the new format intended to address?
options: Members disliking the meeting time
The upstairs room being unavailable
Members refusing to read any chapters
Members having too little time to speak
questions.explanation: Se busca dar más oportunidades de participación.
questions.evidence: Several members said they wanted more time to speak

units.title: Una prueba de trabajo híbrido
units.objective: Interpretar condiciones y el alcance de una decisión provisional.

vocabulary.example: We reached an arrangement to share the storage space.
You may borrow the camera provided you return it tomorrow.
The game allows swaps between players after each round.
The course offers flexibility in choosing assignment topics.

units.strategy: Una prueba no es una política definitiva: escucha las condiciones y la revisión.
units.passage: Next month we will test a hybrid working arrangement. Staff may work from home on two days a week, provided someone from each team is available in the office. This is not a permanent change yet. We will review customer response times and ask staff about their experience after six weeks. Some people have requested fixed home-working days, but managers should allow swaps when caring responsibilities change. The aim is to offer flexibility without making it harder for customers to reach the right person.

questions.prompt: What is the main aim of the trial?
options: To remove all office attendance
To make customer responses less frequent
To balance flexibility with reliable customer access
To give every worker identical fixed days
questions.explanation: El objetivo combina flexibilidad y atención accesible.
questions.evidence: The aim is to offer flexibility without making it harder for customers to reach the right person.

questions.prompt: When will the arrangement be reviewed?
options: After two days
Before next month begins
After a full year
After six weeks
questions.explanation: La revisión ocurre a las seis semanas, no al terminar el primer mes.
questions.evidence: after six weeks

questions.prompt: Why are managers asked to permit swaps?
options: Caring responsibilities can change
All staff dislike working at home
Customers have requested fixed days
The trial is already permanent
questions.explanation: La flexibilidad responde a responsabilidades de cuidado variables.
questions.evidence: managers should allow swaps when caring responsibilities change

units.title: Una exposición para más visitantes
units.objective: Seguir un argumento sobre accesibilidad y una limitación.

vocabulary.example: My favourite exhibit is an old sailing boat.
Radio reception improved when we moved the aerial.
The introductory chapter defines the main terms.
Read the safety instructions before using the tool.

units.strategy: Distingue la mejora concreta de las medidas que todavía no se ofrecen.
units.passage: The museum has introduced an audio guide with shorter descriptions and clearer directions between rooms. We developed it after visitors told us they sometimes lost track of where an exhibit was located. The guide can be downloaded before arrival, which is useful because reception is weak inside the old building. We have not translated every section yet, although the introductory tour is available in three languages. Please send us comments about confusing instructions; we would rather correct them now than keep adding content that is difficult to follow.

questions.prompt: What is the museum prioritising?
options: Adding as many sections as possible immediately
Replacing every exhibit
Making the guide easier to follow
Offering live guides in every room
questions.explanation: La claridad tiene prioridad frente a acumular contenido.
questions.evidence: we would rather correct them now than keep adding content that is difficult to follow

questions.prompt: Why download the guide before arrival?
options: The museum charges more inside
The guide stops working after arrival
The introductory tour is unavailable online
Mobile reception is weak inside
questions.explanation: La descarga previa evita problemas de cobertura.
questions.evidence: reception is weak inside the old building

questions.prompt: What should visitors not assume?
options: That every section is translated
That the introduction has three languages
That comments are welcome
That descriptions are shorter
questions.explanation: Solo se confirma traducción completa para la introducción.
questions.evidence: We have not translated every section yet

units.title: Leer una encuesta con cuidado
units.objective: Interpretar una cautela sobre evidencia y representatividad.

vocabulary.example: The school sent a survey about lunch preferences.
Small businesses are underrepresented on the committee.
The studio equipment was a substantial investment.
The power cut caused widespread disruption.

units.strategy: Busca a quién representa la muestra y qué conclusión se limita.
units.passage: Our survey suggests that residents value the new cycle lanes, but we need to be careful about what the figures tell us. Most responses came through a cycling newsletter, so people who rarely ride may be underrepresented. That does not make the positive comments meaningless; it means they cannot stand for the whole town. Before recommending further investment, we should contact a broader range of residents, including those who travel by bus. I am not proposing that we remove the lanes. I am asking for stronger evidence before claiming that there is widespread support.

questions.prompt: What is the speaker arguing?
options: Delay investment until bus users have approved the existing lanes
Use the positive comments to prioritise the next cycling project
Compare the newsletter’s findings with previous cycling surveys
Collect broader evidence before claiming town-wide support
questions.explanation: La cautela se refiere al alcance de la evidencia, no a rechazar las ciclovías.
questions.evidence: I am asking for stronger evidence before claiming that there is widespread support.

questions.prompt: Why may the responses be unrepresentative?
options: Most came through a cycling newsletter
The questions focused on journeys made during commuting hours
The responses were collected before residents could try the lanes
The results combined views about cycling with views about buses
questions.explanation: Ese canal puede atraer desproporcionadamente a personas que ya van en bicicleta.
questions.evidence: Most responses came through a cycling newsletter

questions.prompt: Why does the speaker say the comments are not meaningless?
options: To suggest that positive views deserve more weight than negative ones
To distinguish limited evidence from worthless evidence
To argue that collecting more responses through the same channel would be sufficient
To defend proceeding with investment while broader research is arranged
questions.explanation: Los comentarios aportan información, pero no representan automáticamente a toda la población.
questions.evidence: That does not make the positive comments meaningless; it means they cannot stand for the whole town.

units.title: Apoyar sin aprobar todavía
units.objective: Reconocer respaldo condicionado y una alternativa viable.

vocabulary.example: Clear navigation helps shoppers find products on a website.
The transition from school to university can take time.
The theatre improved accessibility by installing a lift.
The rollout of the new ticket system will last a month.

units.strategy: However y before often marcan el límite de una aprobación.
units.passage: I can see why the team is excited about the proposed app redesign. The navigation looks simpler, and the larger buttons should help new users. However, the presentation tells us very little about how existing customers would manage the transition. Before we commit to a full release, I would prefer a small trial that includes people who rely on accessibility settings. If that trial identifies only minor problems, we could move quickly. My hesitation is about the rollout, not the design team’s effort, and I hope we can separate those two issues in our discussion.

questions.prompt: How does the speaker view the redesign?
options: Attractive to new users, but probably less useful to existing customers
Ready for release once customers have received written instructions
Worth delaying until the team can demonstrate a faster navigation system
Promising, but needing a carefully tested transition
questions.explanation: La reserva se dirige a la implementación, no a descartar el diseño.
questions.evidence: My hesitation is about the rollout, not the design team’s effort

questions.prompt: Who should be included in the trial?
options: Users who depend on accessibility settings
Customers who have already helped design the larger buttons
Experienced users chosen mainly for their familiarity with the app
New customers recruited before they have seen the current version
questions.explanation: Ese grupo debe participar explícitamente en la prueba.
questions.evidence: includes people who rely on accessibility settings

questions.prompt: Why distinguish rollout from effort?
options: To argue that the effort already invested should influence the release decision
To keep the discussion about implementation rather than personal criticism
To suggest that another team should take responsibility for the trial
To make the case for recognising the designers before discussing customer needs
questions.explanation: Separar ambas cuestiones evita convertir la cautela técnica en un juicio sobre el esfuerzo.
questions.evidence: I hope we can separate those two issues in our discussion

units.title: Qué conserva un archivo
units.objective: Comprender un argumento abstracto mediante un ejemplo concreto.

vocabulary.example: The archive contains recordings of local songs.
The biography has gaps in its account of her childhood.
Several paintings survived the fire.
A joke can be difficult to understand without context.

units.strategy: Identifica el ejemplo y la idea general que demuestra; no los confundas.
units.passage: When we digitise an archive, the temptation is to treat the number of pages scanned as the measure of success. Yet a searchable collection can still conceal important gaps. Letters written by people with stable housing are more likely to have survived than notes passed between temporary workers. If we display both groups as though they were equally documented, we risk presenting absence as evidence of inactivity. The solution is not to invent missing voices, but to explain how the collection was formed and where its limits lie. Access matters, certainly, but access without context can encourage confident misunderstandings.

questions.prompt: What is the central argument?
options: Digital access needs context about the collection’s limitations
Digitisation should prioritise records of groups whose documents are scarce
Search tools should be improved before historical collections are opened
A collection’s success should be measured by how many groups appear in it
questions.explanation: El acceso es valioso, pero requiere explicar límites para evitar interpretaciones engañosas.
questions.evidence: access without context can encourage confident misunderstandings

questions.prompt: Why are temporary workers mentioned?
options: Their notes are harder to search than letters with formal addresses
Their surviving documents may be less numerous
Their documents need more scanning time than the better-preserved letters
Their records were excluded because the archive focuses on settled communities
questions.explanation: El ejemplo contrasta la conservación desigual de documentos; no afirma que nunca escribieran.
questions.evidence: notes passed between temporary workers

questions.prompt: What mistaken inference is the speaker warning against?
options: That gaps can be filled by comparing two groups with different housing histories
That searchable records provide too much context for ordinary readers
That little surviving evidence means little activity
That surviving letters reveal more about housing than about their writers
questions.explanation: Ausencia de documentos no demuestra ausencia de actividad.
questions.evidence: we risk presenting absence as evidence of inactivity

units.title: Una meta que cambia conductas
units.objective: Seguir consecuencias no intencionadas y una propuesta matizada.

vocabulary.example: The fundraising target is nearly within reach.
A careers adviser helped me compare courses.
The discount offers an incentive to book early.
The neighbours resolved their disagreement calmly.

units.strategy: Escucha la diferencia entre mejorar una cifra y mejorar el servicio.
units.passage: The support centre reduced its average call length after introducing a strict time target. On paper, that looked like progress. In practice, some customers had to call twice because their first adviser ended the conversation before resolving the problem. I would not conclude that timing calls is useless; unusually long calls can reveal training needs. But if speed becomes the only signal of quality, staff have an incentive to transfer difficult cases rather than solve them. We should consider whether the issue was resolved alongside how long the call lasted, and review repeated contacts before celebrating the next improvement in the average.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker recommend?
options: Assess resolution as well as call duration
Compare call times only among advisers with similar training
Increase the time target so advisers can handle more complicated requests
Base the next review primarily on the volume of repeated contacts
questions.explanation: Propone combinar tiempo y resolución en lugar de una sola cifra.
questions.evidence: consider whether the issue was resolved alongside how long the call lasted

questions.prompt: What happened to some customers?
options: They waited longer because advisers were receiving additional training
They needed to call again
They were transferred before speaking to their first adviser
They received follow-up calls to confirm that their problem was solved
questions.explanation: La reducción de duración no resolvió siempre el problema a la primera.
questions.evidence: some customers had to call twice

questions.prompt: Why mention training needs?
options: To suggest that inadequate training is the principal cause of repeated calls
To propose training staff to meet the time target more consistently
To acknowledge that call duration can still provide useful information
To show that experienced staff should be exempt from duration monitoring
questions.explanation: Concede utilidad a la métrica, aunque rechaza usarla como único criterio.
questions.evidence: unusually long calls can reveal training needs

units.title: Participación y decisión
units.objective: Interpretar una distinción conceptual y su consecuencia.

vocabulary.example: A public consultation will gather views on the park.
The journal accepted her submission for review.
The route was predetermined before the race began.
The revised timetable includes an extra train.

units.strategy: Sigue la concesión inicial y detecta qué criterio adicional exige quien habla.
units.passage: The consultation was impeccably organised: documents were published on time, meetings were accessible, and every submission received an acknowledgement. Those achievements deserve recognition. Nevertheless, procedural openness is not quite the same as influence. Several participants have asked which proposals changed as a result of their contributions, and the final report is curiously quiet on that point. We need not assume that the decision was predetermined to see why this silence undermines trust. A brief account of what was accepted, rejected, or revised, with reasons, would do more to demonstrate meaningful participation than another round of invitations. The question is not whether people were allowed to speak, but whether the organisation can show how it listened.

questions.prompt: What distinction drives the argument?
options: Receiving an acknowledgement versus being invited to a follow-up meeting
Being allowed to contribute versus demonstrably influencing a decision
Collecting informed proposals versus collecting representative proposals
Explaining a final decision versus allowing participants to make that decision
questions.explanation: Un proceso abierto no demuestra por sí solo que las aportaciones hayan influido.
questions.evidence: procedural openness is not quite the same as influence

questions.prompt: What information does the speaker want published?
options: How the organisation selected participants for accessible meetings
Which contributors submitted the most practical suggestions
How contributions were handled and why
How future consultations will provide more opportunities to speak
questions.explanation: Pide trazabilidad de decisiones, no aceptación automática.
questions.evidence: what was accepted, rejected, or revised, with reasons

questions.prompt: What does “curiously quiet” imply here?
options: The report was intentionally shortened to protect participants’ privacy
The organisation probably considers acknowledgements sufficient evidence of influence
The writer believes the consultation’s decision had already been fixed
The omission deserves scrutiny
questions.explanation: La expresión señala una ausencia llamativa, sin demostrar que hubiera una decisión predeterminada.
questions.evidence: the final report is curiously quiet on that point

units.title: Resultados que no coinciden
units.objective: Entender cautela científica sin confundir discrepancia con refutación total.

vocabulary.example: Another laboratory tried to reproduce the chemical reaction.
The charity recruited volunteers for the festival.
Nobody could predict the outcome of the match.
Can the extra features justify the higher price?

units.strategy: Distingue la observación, las explicaciones posibles y lo que todavía no se puede concluir.
units.passage: The follow-up study failed to reproduce the original improvement, which is disappointing but not, by itself, a verdict on the entire approach. The second team used a shorter training period and recruited participants with substantially more experience. Either difference could have affected the outcome, though pointing to them after the event is not the same as demonstrating that they explain it. Our next study should specify these possibilities in advance and test them directly. Until then, both the enthusiastic claim that the method works everywhere and the dismissive claim that it never works outrun the evidence. A narrower conclusion may attract less attention, but it is the one our results currently justify.

questions.prompt: What position does the speaker defend?
options: The original claim remains the better guide because the follow-up changed the conditions
A limited conclusion pending more targeted research
The method is probably useful only for less experienced participants
The follow-up result should replace the earlier finding until a third study appears
questions.explanation: La conclusión debe ajustarse a lo observado, sin extremos.
questions.evidence: A narrower conclusion may attract less attention, but it is the one our results currently justify.

questions.prompt: How did the second study differ?
options: It selected participants with less prior experience
It extended training to compensate for differences in experience
Its participants had more experience
It tested the same participants after they had completed a second course
questions.explanation: La mayor experiencia y el período más corto son diferencias señaladas.
questions.evidence: recruited participants with substantially more experience

questions.prompt: Why specify possibilities in advance?
options: To remove differences between participant groups before analysing results
To preserve the original interpretation while adapting the training period
To ensure the next team uses precisely the original study’s conditions
To test proposed explanations rather than rely on explanations made afterwards
questions.explanation: Las explicaciones posteriores son hipótesis que todavía requieren una prueba directa.
questions.evidence: specify these possibilities in advance and test them directly

units.title: Eficiencia para quién
units.objective: Identificar supuestos implícitos y redistribución de costes.

vocabulary.example: The map shows the boundaries of the national park.
Successful applicants will receive an interview invitation.
A larger team is not inherently more creative.
Rainfall distribution varies across the region.

units.strategy: Pregunta qué costes entran en la medida y cuáles quedan fuera; no tomes efficiency como una valoración neutral.
units.passage: The proposal is repeatedly described as an efficiency measure, and within the department’s accounting boundaries it may well be one. Moving applications online would reduce processing costs. What remains less visible is the work transferred to applicants who need help completing digital forms, or to community volunteers who supply that help without payment. Calling this a saving is therefore not necessarily false; it is incomplete unless we state whose resources are being counted. I am not suggesting that paper forms are inherently fairer. Rather, the comparison should include the support each system requires and the people expected to provide it. Otherwise, an apparently neutral calculation settles a question of distribution before that question has even been acknowledged.

questions.prompt: What is the speaker challenging?
options: The assumption that online processing itself costs less than paper processing
The proposal to ask applicants rather than staff to choose the application format
The narrow boundaries used to calculate savings
The judgement that unpaid support is necessarily less reliable than paid support
questions.explanation: La crítica apunta a qué recursos se cuentan, no a negar todo ahorro.
questions.evidence: it is incomplete unless we state whose resources are being counted

questions.prompt: Which work may be omitted from the calculation?
options: Training departmental staff to check the completed online forms
Maintaining the software used to process digital applications
Providing paper copies within the department’s existing budget
Unpaid help provided by community volunteers
questions.explanation: Ese trabajo trasladado fuera del departamento puede quedar invisible.
questions.evidence: community volunteers who supply that help without payment

questions.prompt: What is implied by “settles a question of distribution”?
options: A seemingly technical choice can hide a decision about who bears costs
Changing the accounting boundaries would make the two systems cost the same
The apparent saving depends primarily on volunteers working more efficiently
Distribution should be debated only after the cheaper system has been identified
questions.explanation: Elegir los límites del cálculo puede decidir implícitamente quién asume el esfuerzo.
questions.evidence: an apparently neutral calculation settles a question of distribution before that question has even been acknowledged

units.title: Dudar sin renunciar al criterio
units.objective: Seguir una posición matizada frente a dos extremos.

vocabulary.example: On questions of local custom, I defer to my host’s judgement.
The budget came under close scrutiny.
We made a provisional booking while checking our travel dates.
The reviewer never claimed infallibility in her predictions.

units.strategy: Identifica lo que se concede a ambos lados y la condición que sostiene la propuesta final.
units.passage: Public discussions of expertise often leave us with an unhelpful choice: defer without question, or treat every informed judgement as merely another opinion. The first position obscures the assumptions on which advice depends; the second erases the difference between an argument that has survived scrutiny and one that has never faced it. Experts should make their uncertainties legible, but uncertainty is not a blank cheque for any conclusion we happen to prefer. What earns provisional confidence is an account that explains its methods, responds to objections, and changes when contrary evidence warrants it. Such confidence is neither a personal endorsement nor a promise of infallibility. It is a judgement about a process, and it remains open to revision for precisely that reason.

questions.prompt: Which approach does the speaker favour?
options: Trust based principally on the adviser’s established professional reputation
Agreement reached by giving competing judgements comparable weight
Conditional trust in a transparent, revisable process
Confidence reserved for explanations that contain relatively little uncertainty
questions.explanation: La confianza depende de un proceso revisable, no de lealtad personal.
questions.evidence: It is a judgement about a process, and it remains open to revision

questions.prompt: What helps an account earn confidence?
options: Showing that its conclusion is consistent with an established consensus
Reducing objections to those that can be answered with existing methods
Explaining why its previous conclusions were reasonable when first proposed
Explaining methods and responding to objections
questions.explanation: La metodología, la respuesta a críticas y la revisión sustentan confianza provisional.
questions.evidence: explains its methods, responds to objections, and changes when contrary evidence warrants it

questions.prompt: What does “not a blank cheque” reject?
options: Using uncertainty to justify any preferred conclusion
Allowing a conclusion to change before every objection has been answered
Giving confidence to a process rather than to the person applying it
Separating an expert’s advice from the assumptions behind that advice
questions.explanation: Reconocer incertidumbre no vuelve igualmente válida cualquier conclusión deseada.
questions.evidence: uncertainty is not a blank cheque for any conclusion we happen to prefer
